title: Flow-based In Vivo Method to Enumerate Translating Ribosomes and Translation Elongation Rate
author: Mina O. Seedhom

steps.title: Prepare injection solutions and buffers
steps.instruction: Make all required stock solutions and working buffers exactly as described: • CHX stock: dissolve 100 mg cycloheximide in 5 mL 50 % ethanol/50 % water (20 mg/mL); aliquot and store at –20 °C. • PMY stock: dissolve 100 mg puromycin in 2 mL PBS (50 mg/mL); warm to 37 °C, aliquot (usually 1 mL), store at –20 °C. • HAR stock: dissolve 10 mg harringtonine in 200 µL methanol (50 mg/mL); aliquot and store at –20 °C. • Digitonin 1 % stock: dissolve 1 g digitonin in 100 mL DMSO; aliquot and store at –20 °C. • EMA stock (5 mg/mL): dissolve 5 mg EMA in 1 mL DMSO; aliquot and store at –20 °C. • EMA working solution (10 µg/mL): mix 20 µL EMA stock with 10 mL PBS; keep on ice. • Fixation/permeabilization buffer (1 % PFA, 0.0075 % digitonin): combine 9.3 mL PBS, 625 µL 16 % PFA, and 75 µL 1 % digitonin; make fresh and keep on ice. • FACS buffer (0.2 % sodium azide, 1 mg/mL BSA): dissolve 1 g sodium azide and 500 mg BSA in 500 mL PBS; store at 4 °C. • Injection solution A (RPM): prepare 10 mg/mL PMY, 1 mg/mL HAR and 3.4 mg/mL CHX in PBS, warm to 37 °C until PMY fully solubilizes, and make ~20 % extra volume. • Injection solution B (HAR only): prepare 1 mg/mL HAR in PBS, warm if desired, and make ~20 % extra volume.

steps.title: Warm mice and perform IV injections
steps.instruction: Place mice under an ACUC‑approved heat lamp for 5–10 min until activity increases, then restrain each mouse in a holder. Using a 27 G × ½ in. needle attached to a 1 mL syringe, inject 100 µL of the appropriate solution into the tail vein.

substeps.instruction: For a standard RPM assay: inject 100 µL HAR/CHX/PMY solution, then wait 5 min before tissue collection.
Control 1 (background): inject 100 µL HAR solution, wait 15 min, then inject 100 µL HAR/CHX/PMY solution, wait 5 min.
Control 2 (vehicle): inject 100 µL PBS (no PMY) following the same timing.

For ribosome‑transit analysis (RTA): after the initial 100 µL HAR/CHX/PMY injection and 5 min wait, inject 100 µL HAR alone, wait the desired interval (30 s, 1 min, 2 min, 4 min, or 10 min), then inject a second 100 µL HAR/CHX/PMY dose. Include a no‑PMY control as above.

steps.title: Harvest organs into cold medium
steps.instruction: Immediately after the final injection interval, sacrifice each mouse by cervical dislocation. Dissect the organ(s) of interest and place them into a 15 mL conical tube containing 3 mL RPMI 1640 with GlutaMAX supplemented with 7.5 % fetal bovine serum (kept on ice).

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspensions
steps.instruction: All steps are performed on ice with ice‑cold solutions.

substeps.instruction: Crush each organ in 3 mL cold RPMI between two frosted microscope slides placed in a 60 mm × 15 mm cell‑culture dish.
Filter the resulting suspension through a 70 µm mesh into a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 6 mL ACK lysing buffer directly to the filtrate, rotate quickly to lyse red blood cells.
Centrifuge 350 × g for 4 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Tap the tube 3–4 times to break up the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 3 mL cold RPMI + 7.5 % FBS.
Repeat centrifugation (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C), discard supernatant, tap, and resuspend in another 3 mL cold RPMI + 7.5 % FBS.
Filter the suspension again through a 70 µm mesh.
Count cells using a Nexcelom Cellometer Vision with a 1:1 Trypan Blue dilution for live/dead discrimination.
Centrifuge the cell suspension (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C), discard supernatant, tap, and resuspend in cold RPMI + 7.5 % FBS at 10 × 10⁶ cells · mL⁻¹.
Aliquot 200 µL (≈2 × 10⁶ cells) into each well of a 96‑well U‑bottom plate (1–6 × 10⁶ cells per well are acceptable).

steps.title: Live/dead labeling and surface staining
steps.instruction: All staining steps are performed on ice.

substeps.instruction: Prepare single‑color controls (SCC) and fluorescence‑minus‑one (FMO) controls by mixing equal numbers of cells from each organ type.
Add antibodies (Fc block and surface markers) to each well in FACS buffer so that the final volume allows 100 µL per sample; use the dilutions listed in Table 1 (0.75 µL per test for each antibody).
Centrifuge the 96‑well plate at 350 × g for 4 min at 4 °C; verify a solid pellet has formed.
Resuspend cells in 200 µL PBS with a multichannel pipette, then centrifuge again (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C).
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 µL of 10 µg/mL EMA solution (prepared above). Incubate 10 min on ice in the dark.
Expose the uncovered plate to a fluorescent light source (465–475 nm) for an additional 10 min on ice (commercial fluorescent lamp or PMA‑Lite 2.0 LED).
Add 100 µL PBS, mix, and centrifuge (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C).
Wash twice with 200 µL PBS.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL FACS buffer containing the Fc‑blocking antibody (2.42G monoclonal, diluted as per manufacturer) and incubate 10 min on ice.
Add 100 µL of the appropriate surface‑antibody cocktail (SCC, FMO, or full panel) at the dilutions given in Table 1; incubate 30 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C) and wash twice with 200 µL PBS.

steps.title: Fix, permeabilize and stain intracellular puromycin

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL freshly prepared fixation/permeabilization buffer (1 % PFA, 0.0075 % digitonin in PBS) to each well; incubate 20 min at 4 °C.
Add 100 µL PBS, centrifuge (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C), and wash twice with PBS.
Add conjugated anti‑puromycin antibody at 1:100 dilution (e.g., 1 µL antibody to 100 µL buffer) and incubate 1 h at 4 °C (or overnight if preferred).
Add 100 µL PBS, pipette up‑and‑down 6–8 times, then centrifuge (350 × g, 4 min, 4 °C).
Wash twice with 200 µL PBS, resuspend the final cell pellet in FACS buffer, keep on ice.
Samples may be stored in a dark refrigerator (4 °C) for up to 1 week before acquisition.

steps.title: Acquire data on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Run the stained samples on a flow cytometer (e.g., BD LSRII or BD LSR Fortessa X‑20) keeping them on ice during acquisition; use the SCC and FMO controls for gating and compensation.
